item.title: J&J told to pay $9 million in talc-related cancer case as appeals court upholds award
item.description: A Louisiana appeals court has upheld a $9.07 million damages award against Johnson & Johnson in a case involving Jeannine Henderson, who developed mesothelioma after decades of using the company's talcum powder products. Her family argued that asbestos in the products contributed to her illness, while J&J blamed exposure from an industrial area near her home. The court rejected the company's appeal and left the compensation awarded to her two sons unchanged. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A non-venomous snake that does not constrict its prey can still kill with its bite
item.description: Recent studies on Drymarchon snakes reveal their impressive biting ability, which they utilize to capture prey with remarkable efficiency. Unlike typical assumptions about non-venomous species, these snakes can exert bite pressures surpassing those of their constrictor counterparts. The research highlights how their jaw anatomy facilitates this concentrated force, emphasizing that their success also hinges on maintaining grip post-bite. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
